description: Java AWT (Abstract Window Toolkit) class is a set of classes and methods used to create and manage graphical user interface (GUI) components, such as windows, buttons, and menus, in Java applications. name: Java Class Batch
full_name: System Interaction##Batch Services##Script Batch Interfaces##Java Batch Processing##Java Class Batch
description: In Java, a Batch class typically refers to a class that contains the configuration for a batch job in a batch processing system. It defines the steps and processing logic for the batch job, such as reading data, processing it, and writing the results. Batch classes are used to automate and manage the execution of batch jobs in Java applications.

name: Java Class DAO
full_name: Services##Logic Services##Data Access Services##Java Data Access##Java Class DAO
description: A Java DAO (Data Access Object) class is a class that provides an abstract interface to some type of database or other persistence mechanism. It typically contains methods for performing CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations on data objects. DAO classes abstract the details of accessing the database and provide a clean separation between business logic and data access code. They are commonly used in enterprise applications to manage data access operations.

name: Java Class EJB
full_name: Services##Logic Services##Business Logic Communication##Java Communication##Java Class EJB
description: A Java EJB (Enterprise JavaBean) class is a server-side component that encapsulates business logic in a distributed Java EE application. EJBs provide services such as transaction management, security, and concurrency control, making them suitable for enterprise-level applications. They are annotated with @Stateless, @Stateful, or @MessageDriven to define their behavior and are managed by the EJB container. EJBs promote modularity and reusability by allowing developers to focus on business logic rather than infrastructure concerns.
